answer: Grader-correlation anomaly detection resists sybil rings: independent honest graders legitimately disagree on contested items, so their pairwise agreement carries bounded, noisy entropy across the open meadow of real judgment. A collusion ring instead emits near-perfect mutual agreement on the items it shares, a karst-rigid low-entropy signature. The protocol measures concord only where honest verdicts genuinely vary, weights it by shared assignments, and flags grader subsets whose agreement climbs to an improbable summit. Rings that rubber-stamp in lockstep mark themselves.
